newsitem.title: USA: Northeast CFO says 1997 "break even at best".
newsitem.headline: Northeast CFO says 1997 "break even at best".

text.p: Northeast Utilities Chief Financial Officer John Forsgren, speaking here at the Connecticut-based utility's annual shareholders meeting, said "1997 will be a break even year for the company at best."
Forsgren told shareholders that Northeast's nuclear problems were "extremely costly."

"As you know, these costs are taking an enormous toll on our earnings," he said, adding that the company is spending about $30 million a month to buy electricity that otherwise would have been produced at its Millstone nuclear power station.
He said Northeast also expects to spend more than $200 million this year to try to bring the three Millstone plants back on line.
The three units, in Waterford, Conn., have an overall generating capacity of about 2,700 megawatts. They have been shut since early 1996 amid safety concerns.
In addition, Northeast is spending $70 million this year to help meet customers' summer and winter demand for electricity.
"I know this is not pleasant news, but it is the challenge we must deal with this year, and we are dealing with it successfully," Forsgren said.
